accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the type of robot?
o: Surgical robot — robotic surgery and rehabilitation
accepted.x: Surgical or medical robots are used in robotic surgery and rehabilitation. Industrial robots are associated with assembly, welding and painting, while service robots serve functions such as hospitality and reception.
accepted.tq: Match the robot category with its characteristic application.
accepted.sec: ■ Robotics - types, Indian robots → developer + purpose, standards bodies  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Cobots, increasingly used in Indian factories, are designed primarily to:
o: Replace all human workers in hazardous industries
accepted.x: Cobots, or collaborative robots, are designed to work alongside humans. They are distinct from robots intended to operate independently in isolated environments.
accepted.tq: Identify the defining function of the specialised term.
accepted.sec: ■ Robotics - types, Indian robots → developer + purpose, standards bodies  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. HomoSEP — IIT Madras
2. Vyommitra — ISRO
3. Daksh — DRDO
4. Manav — Genrobotics
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: HomoSEP was developed by IIT Madras, Vyommitra by ISRO and Daksh by DRDO. Manav was developed by A-SET Training & Research Institutes, Delhi, not Genrobotics.
accepted.tq: Check each developer association and eliminate the swapped organisation.
accepted.sec: ■ Robotics - types, Indian robots → developer + purpose, standards bodies  [APPSC]

accepted.s: HomoSEP is associated with which of the following purposes?
o: Supporting an uncrewed space mission as an astronaut
accepted.x: HomoSEP, developed by IIT Madras, is intended for septic-tank cleaning. Daksh handles IEDs and bombs, whereas Vyommitra is associated with the uncrewed Gaganyaan flight.
accepted.tq: Link the named robot with its specific purpose.
accepted.sec: ■ Robotics - types, Indian robots → developer + purpose, standards bodies  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Vyommitra, developed by ISRO, is described as a:
o: Half-humanoid astronaut for the uncrewed Gaganyaan flight
accepted.x: Vyommitra is ISRO’s half-humanoid astronaut intended for the uncrewed Gaganyaan flight.
accepted.tq: Use the purpose and developer together to identify the correct robot.
accepted.sec: ■ Robotics - types, Indian robots → developer + purpose, standards bodies  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Daksh is a remotely operated robot developed by DRDO for:
o: Handling and defusing IEDs and bombs
Creating digital layers over physical surroundings
accepted.x: Daksh was developed by DRDO as a remotely operated robot for handling and defusing IEDs and bombs.
accepted.tq: Distinguish robots by their operational purpose rather than by their names.
accepted.sec: ■ Robotics - types, Indian robots → developer + purpose, standards bodies  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Manav, associated with A-SET Training & Research Institutes, Delhi, is notable as India’s first:
accepted.x: Manav was developed by A-SET Training & Research Institutes, Delhi, and is described as India’s first 3D-printed humanoid in 2017.
accepted.tq: Test the distinctive achievement attached to the named robot.
accepted.sec: ■ Robotics - types, Indian robots → developer + purpose, standards bodies  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which organisation is associated with the development of the Bandicoot robot?
accepted.x: Bandicoot was developed by Genrobotics of Kerala for manhole and sewer cleaning, helping to end manual scavenging.
accepted.tq: Identify the developer from a set of closely related Indian robotics institutions.
accepted.sec: ■ Robotics - types, Indian robots → developer + purpose, standards bodies  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The ISO Technical Committee 299 is concerned with standards relating to:
accepted.x: ISO Technical Committee 299 deals with robotics. ISO 10218 is associated with safety requirements for industrial robots.
accepted.tq: Match the standards committee with its field.
accepted.sec: ■ Robotics - types, Indian robots → developer + purpose, standards bodies  [APPSC]

accepted.s: ISO 10218 is associated with norms concerning:
accepted.x: ISO 10218 lays down standards related to industrial-robot safety under the robotics standards framework.
accepted.tq: Use the standard number to identify the specific regulatory subject.
accepted.sec: ■ Robotics - types, Indian robots → developer + purpose, standards bodies  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the institutional support for robotics in India is correct?
o: The MeitY inter-ministerial committee has the Secretary, MeitY, as its convener.
Robotics is excluded from the Technology Innovation Hubs under NM-ICPS.
The committee is convened by the Secretary of the Ministry of Heavy Industries.
Robotics is one of the verticals of only five Technology Innovation Hubs.
accepted.x: MeitY set up an inter-ministerial committee to build a robotics ecosystem, with the Secretary, MeitY, as convener. Robotics is also one of the verticals of the 25 Technology Innovation Hubs under NM-ICPS.
accepted.tq: Find the correct authority and verify the numerical composition.
accepted.sec: ■ Robotics - types, Indian robots → developer + purpose, standards bodies  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Internet of Things (IoT) refers to:
o: A network limited to industrial robots
Only computers connected through wired networks
A system in which data can be exchanged only after manual approval
Devices with sensors linked in a network and exchanging data without human intervention
accepted.x: IoT consists of sensor-equipped devices connected through networks that exchange data without human intervention.
accepted.tq: Select the precise definition and reject restrictive qualifiers such as ‘only’.
accepted.sec: ■ Internet of Things - full form, layers, applications  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the three-layer model of the Internet of Things, from the device-facing layer to the user-facing layer?
accepted.x: The three-layer IoT model consists of the perception layer, network layer and application layer. The perception layer senses, the network layer transmits and the application layer provides smart services.
accepted.tq: Recall the ordered layers and their functional progression.
accepted.sec: ■ Internet of Things - full form, layers, applications  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In the three-layer IoT model, the perception layer primarily includes:
accepted.x: The perception layer contains devices such as sensors and RFID systems that collect information from the physical environment.
accepted.tq: Match each layer with the function performed at that stage.
accepted.sec: ■ Internet of Things - full form, layers, applications  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Internet of Mobile Things — mass production assembly lines
accepted.x: Internet of Mobile Things concerns mobile devices or mobile objects. Industrial automation is associated with IIoT, nano-devices with IoNT and military applications with mission-critical IoT.
accepted.tq: Find the mismatched variant by comparing each abbreviation with its field.
accepted.sec: ■ Internet of Things - full form, layers, applications  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is the odd one out in relation to common IoT applications?
accepted.x: Smart farming, smart grids and smart cities are IoT applications. Manual typewriter servicing is not identified as an IoT application.
accepted.tq: Separate the listed technology-enabled applications from the unrelated activity.
accepted.sec: ■ Internet of Things - full form, layers, applications  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The four pillars identified for IoT are:
accepted.x: The four IoT pillars are device, data, analytics and connectivity.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact components of a named framework.
accepted.sec: ■ Internet of Things - full form, layers, applications  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The IoT Centres of Excellence established through the MeitY-NASSCOM initiative are located at:
accepted.x: The MeitY-NASSCOM IoT Centres of Excellence are located at Bengaluru, Gurugram, Gandhinagar and Visakhapatnam.
accepted.tq: Check the complete location list rather than identifying only one familiar city.
accepted.sec: ■ Internet of Things - full form, layers, applications  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the role of the mMTC slice in 5G?
o: It serves dense deployments of IoT sensors.
It is used exclusively for high-definition video streaming.
It replaces all network security functions.
It is designed only for satellite communication.
accepted.x: mMTC means massive machine-type communication and is intended to support dense IoT sensor deployments in 5G networks.
accepted.tq: Apply the expansion and purpose of the communication category to the scenario.
accepted.sec: ■ Internet of Things - full form, layers, applications  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding IoT and AI:
1. IoT devices collect and exchange data through sensors.
2. AI analyses data, recognises patterns and makes decisions.
3. A smart thermostat is an example listed under AI rather than IoT.
4. Chatbots and image recognition are examples associated with AI.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. A smart thermostat is listed as an IoT example, whereas chatbots and image recognition are associated with AI.
accepted.tq: Separate data collection and exchange from analysis, pattern recognition and decision-making.
accepted.sec: ■ Internet of Things - full form, layers, applications  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The defining technology of Industry 1.0 was:
accepted.x: Industry 1.0 was characterised by mechanisation, steam power and the weaving loom.
accepted.tq: Use the stage number to identify the corresponding industrial technology.
accepted.sec: ■ Industrial revolutions 1.0 to 4.0, Industry 5.0, SAMARTH Udyog Bharat 4.0  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the sequence of defining technologies from Industry 1.0 to Industry 4.0?
o: Steam power — electricity — computers and electronics — cyber-physical systems
Electricity — steam power — cyber-physical systems — computers
Computers — electricity — steam power — artificial intelligence
Cyber-physical systems — steam power — electricity — computers
accepted.x: Industry 1.0 involved steam-powered mechanisation; Industry 2.0 electricity and mass production; Industry 3.0 computers and electronics; and Industry 4.0 cyber-physical systems.
accepted.tq: Arrange the stages by their defining technological progression.
accepted.sec: ■ Industrial revolutions 1.0 to 4.0, Industry 5.0, SAMARTH Udyog Bharat 4.0  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Industry 2.0 is principally associated with:
o: Human-machine collaboration at the centre of innovation
Electricity, mass production and the assembly line
accepted.x: Industry 2.0 introduced electricity, mass production and the assembly line. Steam power belongs to Industry 1.0, while cyber-physical systems belong to Industry 4.0.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between adjacent industrial stages using their hallmark technologies.
accepted.sec: ■ Industrial revolutions 1.0 to 4.0, Industry 5.0, SAMARTH Udyog Bharat 4.0  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following are characteristic features of Industry 4.0?
1. Cyber-physical systems
2. Internet of Things and networks
3. Artificial intelligence and big data
4. Steam-powered weaving looms
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Industry 4.0 is characterised by cyber-physical systems, IoT, networks, AI and big data. Steam-powered weaving looms belong to Industry 1.0.
accepted.tq: Identify the stage-specific technologies and reject a feature from an earlier revolution.
accepted.sec: ■ Industrial revolutions 1.0 to 4.0, Industry 5.0, SAMARTH Udyog Bharat 4.0  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The term ‘Fourth Industrial Revolution’ was coined by:
o: The Secretary, Ministry of Heavy Industries
Klaus Schwab, founder of the World Economic Forum
The Director-General of the International Labour Organization
accepted.x: Klaus Schwab, founder of the World Economic Forum, coined the term ‘Fourth Industrial Revolution’ in 2016.
accepted.tq: Link the phrase with its originator and the associated institution.
accepted.sec: ■ Industrial revolutions 1.0 to 4.0, Industry 5.0, SAMARTH Udyog Bharat 4.0  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Fourth Industrial Revolution is described as the convergence of:
o: Mechanical, chemical and legal systems only
Agricultural, maritime and linguistic technologies only
accepted.x: The Fourth Industrial Revolution involves the convergence of digital, physical and biological technologies and is associated with smart factories.
accepted.tq: Recall the precise three-part conceptual description.
accepted.sec: ■ Industrial revolutions 1.0 to 4.0, Industry 5.0, SAMARTH Udyog Bharat 4.0  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which statement best expresses the central emphasis of Industry 5.0?
o: Replacement of digital systems by manual assembly lines
Human-machine collaboration with people at the centre of innovation
Complete exclusion of humans from industrial production
accepted.x: Industry 5.0 places people at the centre of industrial innovation and emphasises collaboration between humans and machines.
accepted.tq: Identify the conceptual shift from automation-centred production to human-machine collaboration.
accepted.sec: ■ Industrial revolutions 1.0 to 4.0, Industry 5.0, SAMARTH Udyog Bharat 4.0  [APPSC]

accepted.s: SAMARTH Udyog Bharat 4.0 is best described as:
o: A Ministry of Heavy Industries initiative to spread Industry 4.0 through demonstration centres
An ISRO programme for humanoid astronauts
A MeitY programme limited to biometric authentication
A DRDO programme for bomb-disposal robots
accepted.x: SAMARTH Udyog Bharat 4.0, meaning Smart Advanced Manufacturing and Rapid Transformation Hub, is a Ministry of Heavy Industries initiative that promotes Industry 4.0 through demonstration centres.
accepted.tq: Match the initiative with its ministry and implementation mechanism.
accepted.sec: ■ Industrial revolutions 1.0 to 4.0, Industry 5.0, SAMARTH Udyog Bharat 4.0  [APPSC]

accepted.s: RFID communication primarily takes place through radio waves exchanged between:
o: A satellite and a television broadcaster only
A biometric sensor and a printer only
A battery and a display screen
A tag carrying identity data and a reader
accepted.x: RFID uses radio waves between a tag, which carries identity data, and a reader.
accepted.tq: Identify the two essential components and the communication medium.
accepted.sec: ■ RFID and wearables - passive vs active tags, wearable functions  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes an active RFID tag?
o: It has its own battery and transmitter and can broadcast itself over a long range.
It stores no identity data and functions only as a visual label.
Its battery powers only the chip and it must use the reader’s field to reply.
It has no battery and only reflects the reader’s field over a short range.
accepted.x: An active RFID tag has its own battery and transmitter, broadcasts by itself and generally offers a longer range. A semi-passive tag uses its battery for the chip but relies on the reader’s field to reply.
accepted.tq: Distinguish active, passive and semi-passive tags by their power source and response method.
accepted.sec: ■ RFID and wearables - passive vs active tags, wearable functions  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A semi-passive RFID tag differs from an active RFID tag because the semi-passive tag:
o: Uses its battery to run the chip but uses the reader’s field to reply
Has no internal power and cannot contain identity data
Has an independent transmitter and broadcasts over a long range
Uses only a satellite signal for communication
accepted.x: A semi-passive tag’s battery powers its chip, but it still uses the reader’s field to send its response. An active tag has its own battery and transmitter.
accepted.tq: Focus on the exact distinction between battery use and transmission capability.
accepted.sec: ■ RFID and wearables - passive vs active tags, wearable functions  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following functions are commonly performed by wearable devices such as smartwatches and fitness bands?
1. Tracking heart rate, steps and sleep
2. Biometric authentication
3. Acting as typical IoT end-devices
4. Producing steam power for industrial machinery
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Wearables track health and fitness indicators, support biometric authentication and function as typical IoT end-devices. They do not produce steam power for industrial machinery.
accepted.tq: Separate genuine wearable functions from an unrelated industrial-revolution feature.
accepted.sec: ■ RFID and wearables - passive vs active tags, wearable functions  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Augmented Reality — digital layers over the real world
Mixed Reality — a completely isolated computer-generated world
Extended Reality — only physical objects without digital content
Metaverse — a non-persistent two-dimensional text file
accepted.x: Augmented Reality overlays digital content on the real world. Mixed Reality allows real and virtual objects to interact in real time, while Extended Reality is the umbrella term for VR, AR and MR.
accepted.tq: Match each extended-reality term with its defining characteristic.
accepted.sec: ■ Extended reality - VR, AR, MR, metaverse  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In Mixed Reality, the defining feature is that:
o: The physical world is completely excluded
The user receives data only through an RFID reader
Real and virtual objects interact in real time
Only printed images are displayed without digital content
accepted.x: Mixed Reality combines real and virtual elements so that real and virtual objects can interact in real time.
accepted.tq: Distinguish mixed reality from the overlay-only nature of augmented reality.
accepted.sec: ■ Extended reality - VR, AR, MR, metaverse  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Extended Reality (XR) is an umbrella term covering:
o: Smart grids, smart homes and smart farming only
accepted.x: Extended Reality is the umbrella category comprising Virtual Reality, Augmented Reality and Mixed Reality.
accepted.tq: Expand the umbrella concept by identifying all of its constituent technologies.
accepted.sec: ■ Extended reality - VR, AR, MR, metaverse  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following best describes the metaverse?
o: A wearable device that measures heart rate alone
A physical assembly line controlled only by steam power
A persistent, shared three-dimensional virtual space using XR, avatars and digital assets
accepted.x: The metaverse is a persistent and shared 3D virtual space that uses extended reality, avatars and digital assets.
accepted.tq: Select the comprehensive definition rather than a single enabling technology.
accepted.sec: ■ Extended reality - VR, AR, MR, metaverse  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Pokémon Go is commonly cited as an example of:
accepted.x: Pokémon Go overlays digital elements on the real-world environment and is therefore an example of Augmented Reality.
accepted.tq: Apply the technology definition to a familiar real-world example.
accepted.sec: ■ Extended reality - VR, AR, MR, metaverse  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The VARCoE (VR/AR Centre of Excellence) is located at:
accepted.x: The VARCoE is located at IIT Bhubaneswar and is associated with MeitY, STPI and Odisha.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the centre’s location from the separate Hyderabad-based IMAGE CoE.
accepted.sec: ■ Extended reality - VR, AR, MR, metaverse  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The IMAGE Centre of Excellence is associated with which location and fields?
o: Hyderabad; gaming, VFX, computer vision and AI
Visakhapatnam; smart farming and smart grids
Delhi; space robotics and uncrewed launch vehicles
accepted.x: The IMAGE CoE is located at Hyderabad and focuses on gaming, visual effects, computer vision and artificial intelligence. It is associated with MeitY, STPI and Telangana.
accepted.tq: Use both location and subject area to distinguish closely related Centres of Excellence.
accepted.sec: ■ Extended reality - VR, AR, MR, metaverse  [APPSC]
